issues.t: Passenger airbag inflator can rupture (recall)
issues.sym: Usually nothing you can notice. The danger only appears if the front passenger airbag goes off in a crash.
issues.why: The RL's Takata passenger airbag inflator can break down after years of heat and humidity. When it fires, the metal housing can burst and throw sharp fragments into the cabin. Acura has run several recalls on these inflators. NHTSA recall numbers: 14V-700, 16V-344, 17V-029, 19V-501.
issues.next: Run your VIN through Acura's or NHTSA's recall lookup today. If a passenger inflator recall is open, book the free replacement and keep people out of the front passenger seat until it is done.

issues.t: Driver airbag inflator can rupture (recall)
issues.sym: No warning signs before a crash. The problem only shows up when the steering wheel airbag deploys.
issues.why: Moisture can get into the driver's dual-stage Takata inflator over time, and the aged propellant can burn too fast and split the inflator housing when the airbag fires.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open airbag recalls and have the free driver inflator replacement done as soon as the dealer can fit you in. NHTSA recall numbers: 16V-061, 19V-500.

issues.t: Older driver airbag inflator can rupture (recall)
issues.sym: Nothing to notice day to day. The fault only matters if the driver airbag deploys.
issues.why: The driver airbag inflators in these older RLs (including some replacement units) can absorb moisture and then rupture or underinflate the bag in a crash.
issues.next: Look up the VIN for open recalls and get the free inflator inspection or replacement. This applies even if the car has had an airbag replaced before. NHTSA recall number: 20V-026.

issues.t: Front lower ball joints can wear and separate (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking from the front end over bumps, loose or wandering steering, or uneven front tire wear. In the worst case the front wheel can fold under the car.
issues.why: The front lower ball joints on early RLs could wear out faster than normal. A badly worn joint can pull apart and collapse the front suspension.
issues.next: If you hear clunks from the front, stop driving fast and have the ball joints checked. Confirm the recall replacement was done on your VIN. NHTSA recall number: 99V-069.

issues.t: Transmission case bolt can loosen and lose Park (recall)
issues.sym: The car may lose drive or may roll even with the shifter in Park.
issues.why: A bolt inside the automatic transmission case can work loose. When it does, the parking mechanism and gear engagement can stop working properly.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake until you confirm the recall was done. A dealer installs a redesigned bolt for free. NHTSA recall number: 99V-227.

issues.t: Harsh or delayed shift from 1st to 2nd gear
issues.sym: A bump, shudder or clunk when the automatic shifts from first to second, often worse when the car is cold. Some cars hum or whine in certain gears.
issues.why: Acura issued several service bulletins for 1-2 shift complaints on these RLs. Worn or dirty transmission fluid and internal wear make it worse. Leaks of transmission fluid were also covered by a bulletin.
issues.next: Check the transmission fluid level and color. Have a shop drain and refill with genuine Honda ATF and check for codes before deciding on bigger repairs.

issues.t: Engine starts then dies when the key is released
issues.sym: The engine fires up while you hold the key in Start, then stalls as soon as you let go to the Run position.
issues.why: Acura's bulletins point to the ignition switch, which can wear so the Run position no longer powers the engine systems after the starter is released.
issues.next: Have the ignition switch tested. Replacing the switch usually fixes it, so test it before chasing fuel or ignition parts.

issues.t: A/C stops cooling or the compressor fails
issues.sym: Warm air from the vents, weak cooling when you accelerate hard, or a noisy A/C compressor that eventually quits.
issues.why: Owners report A/C compressor failures on these RLs, sometimes more than once. Acura also released bulletins on compressor control logic and poor cooling under hard acceleration.
issues.next: Have the A/C system checked for leaks and pressures before refilling. If the compressor has failed, flushing the system and replacing the receiver-dryer helps the new one last.

issues.t: SRS airbag warning light stays on
issues.sym: The airbag (SRS) light stays lit on the dash, sometimes along with other warning lights.
issues.why: Faulty airbag sensors are the most common problem RepairPal lists for the RL. Acura bulletins cover SRS codes from the passenger position sensor, the driver inflator circuit and the SRS control unit itself.
issues.next: Have the SRS codes read with a proper scan tool. The airbags may not work correctly while the light is on, so do not ignore it.

issues.t: Check engine light from an EVAP leak code
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with no change in how the car drives. A scan shows P1456 or P1457.
issues.why: These codes point to a leak in the fuel vapor (EVAP) system. A binding or worn gas cap and a failed EVAP bypass solenoid are common causes, and Acura issued bulletins for both.
issues.next: First check that the gas cap clicks tight and the seal is not cracked. If the light comes back, have the EVAP system smoke-tested.

issues.t: Cranks but won't start with the immobilizer light flashing
issues.sym: The engine turns over but will not fire, or starts and dies, and the green key (immobilizer) light blinks.
issues.why: The anti-theft immobilizer is not recognizing the key, which can come from a damaged key chip, a weak key, or a fault in the immobilizer system. Acura issued bulletins for this on several model years.
issues.next: Try your spare key first. If the spare works, the original key needs replacing. If neither works, a dealer or locksmith with the right tool can check the immobilizer.

issues.t: Brake lights may not work from a contaminated switch (recall)
issues.sym: Brake lights that stay off or work only some of the time when you press the pedal.
issues.why: Oil left over from manufacturing could get onto the brake light switch and stop it from making contact. Drivers behind you then get no warning when you slow down.
issues.next: Have someone watch the brake lights while you press the pedal. If they fail, get the free recall repair, which cleans the pedal area and replaces the switch. NHTSA recall number: 02V-119.

issues.t: Corroded brake master cylinder reduces braking (recall)
issues.sym: A brake pedal that sinks lower than normal or a car that takes longer to stop.
issues.why: The inside of the brake master cylinder on some 2000 RLs could corrode, which lowers the pressure it sends to the brakes.
issues.next: If the brake pedal sinks, feels soft or goes closer to the floor, or a red brake warning comes on, slow down gently, use a lower gear, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on: call for a tow. If the pedal feels low or soft, have the brakes checked right away. Confirm the recall master cylinder replacement was done. NHTSA recall number: 03V-239.

issues.t: Power steering hose can crack and leak (recall)
issues.sym: Power steering fluid drips under the front of the car, a burning smell, whining steering, or steering that gets heavy.
issues.why: Engine heat can make the power steering hose crack. Leaking fluid can land on hot engine parts and, in rare cases, catch fire.
issues.next: If you smell burning fluid or see a leak, stop and have it checked. The recall replaces the hose with a heat-resistant one for free. NHTSA recall number: 07V-551.

issues.t: Stability control can brake on its own (recall)
issues.sym: The car brakes or pulls without you pressing the pedal, possibly with the VSA warning light on.
issues.why: A capacitor in the vehicle stability assist (VSA) module can be damaged and a ground connection can be loose. That can make the system apply the brakes when it should not.
issues.next: Check that the recall was done on your VIN. Under the recall, the dealer installs a new wiring harness and tightens the ground. NHTSA recall number: 13V-092.

issues.t: Fuel pump relay can fail and stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stalls while driving or will not start because the fuel pump gets no power.
issues.why: A coil wire inside the fuel pump relay can break, cutting power to the fuel pump.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. If your 2005 RL stalls without warning, have the recall checked. The dealer replaces the relay for free. NHTSA recall number: 07V-097.

issues.t: Brake master cylinder seal can leak (recall)
issues.sym: Low brake fluid, a brake warning light, or a brake pedal that slowly sinks.
issues.why: Some service brake fluid without the right additives could dry out a seal in the master cylinder, letting fluid leak past it.
issues.next: If the brake pedal sinks, feels soft or goes closer to the floor, or a red brake warning comes on, slow down gently, use a lower gear, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on: call for a tow. Watch the brake fluid level and pedal feel. Have the free recall seal replacement done and use only Honda/Acura-approved brake fluid. NHTSA recall number: 10V-504.

issues.t: Doors won't lock or unlock from the handle sensor
issues.sym: Touching the door handle no longer unlocks or locks the car with the smart key, or the doors lock at random while driving.
issues.why: The touch sensors in the outer door handles fail on these RLs. Acura also issued a bulletin saying water leaking into the door can damage the circuit so the doors stop unlocking.
issues.next: Use the key fob buttons in the meantime. A shop can test the handle sensor and check for water inside the door before replacing parts.

issues.t: Engine shudder or no shift into 4th gear
issues.sym: A shudder while cruising, or the automatic will not upshift into fourth gear.
issues.why: Acura found the engine computer software on early 2005 RLs could cause the shudder and block the upshift. Updated software was released.
issues.next: Ask an Acura dealer to check whether the PCM software update has been done. It is a quick reflash rather than a transmission repair.

issues.t: Torque converter judder while cruising
issues.sym: A shudder or rumble like driving over rumble strips, usually at steady speeds with light throttle.
issues.why: The lock-up clutch in the torque converter can grab unevenly. Acura released a software update and extended the warranty on the torque converter.
issues.next: Ask a dealer about the software update and whether the extended torque converter coverage still applies to your car.

issues.t: Navigation clock or date shows the wrong time
issues.sym: The clock reads the wrong time or 00:00, or the navigation shows the wrong date.
issues.why: The GPS receiver in the navigation unit has a date counter that rolled over, so it calculates the wrong time and date. Acura issued bulletins for it.
issues.next: This does not affect how the car drives. Ask a dealer whether a fix or update is available for your navigation unit.

issues.t: Fuel pump can fail and stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine may run rough, refuse to start, or stall while driving.
issues.why: The impeller inside the in-tank fuel pump can swell and rub until the pump stops working. Acura has recalled these pumps.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check the VIN for open fuel pump recalls. If the engine sputters or stalls, get off the road safely and have the car towed to a dealer.

issues.t: Early RLX fuel pump can fail (recall)
issues.sym: Hard starting, a rough-running engine, or a stall while driving.
issues.why: The in-tank fuel pump in some early RLXs can fail, which cuts fuel to the engine.
issues.next: Look up your VIN for open recalls. Under the recall, the dealer replaces the fuel pump module. NHTSA recall number: 23V-858.

issues.t: Timing belt teeth can separate (recall)
issues.sym: The engine can suddenly stall and not restart.
issues.why: Some timing belts were made with teeth that can peel off the belt. If that happens the engine loses timing and stops.
issues.next: Confirm the recall was done. The dealer replaces the belt and checks the engine for damage free of charge.

issues.t: Collision braking may brake for guardrails (recall)
issues.sym: The car brakes hard on its own when passing roadside metal fences or guardrails.
issues.why: The collision mitigation braking system could mistake roadside metal barriers for an obstacle ahead and apply the brakes.
issues.next: Have the free software update done. Until then, stay alert to unexpected braking on roads lined with guardrails. NHTSA recall number: 15V-301.

issues.t: Headlight reflector can peel and dim the lights (recall)
issues.sym: Headlights look dim or throw less light down the road at night.
issues.why: A thin aluminum coating inside the headlight reflector can peel away, so less light is reflected forward.
issues.next: If your headlights seem weak, check for the open recall. The dealer replaces both headlights for free. NHTSA recall number: 14V-792.

issues.t: Front seat belts may not extend or retract in cold weather (recall)
issues.sym: In cold weather, the driver or passenger seat belt will not pull out or wind back in.
issues.why: The front seat belt retractors in some 2014 RLXs can stick in low temperatures.
issues.next: Check for the open recall. Under the recall, the dealer replaces both front seat belts. NHTSA recall number: 14V-639.

issues.t: Moaning or rubbing noise from the rear while steering
issues.sym: A moan, groan or rubbing sound from the back of the car when driving straight or making small steering corrections.
issues.why: Acura traced it to manufacturing errors in rear steering and suspension parts and issued a service bulletin and a warranty extension.
issues.next: Ask an Acura dealer whether your car is covered by the warranty extension before paying for any repair.

issues.t: Torque converter shudder at 20-60 mph
issues.sym: A vibration or shudder like rumble strips when cruising at roughly 20 to 60 mph.
issues.why: The torque converter lock-up clutch can judder as the transmission fluid ages. Acura's bulletins call for updated software and fresh fluid, and warn the shudder can return if the fluid breaks down again.
issues.next: Ask a dealer about the transmission software update and a fluid change before anyone replaces the torque converter.

issues.t: Rough running at cruise with a flashing check engine light
issues.sym: The engine rattles or runs rough at a steady 30 to 65 mph and the check engine light blinks.
issues.why: Acura linked this to the Variable Cylinder Management system, which shuts off some cylinders at cruise to save fuel.
issues.next: If the check engine light flashes, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off. Ask the dealer about the related bulletin and software update.

issues.t: Chirp from the timing belt area after warm-up
issues.sym: A chirping or squeaking noise from the front of the engine once it is warm.
issues.why: Acura says the timing belt can rub against the back edge of the crankshaft pulley.
issues.next: Ask the dealer about the timing belt chirp bulletin. Have it looked at during your next service so it is not confused with a failing belt or pulley.

issues.t: Check engine light for misfire or lean codes
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on, sometimes with a rough idle or hesitation. A scan shows misfire codes (P030X) or lean codes (P0171, P0174).
issues.why: Acura opened a technical investigation into certain 2016-2020 MDX, RLX and TLX V6 models with these codes.
issues.next: Have the codes read and ask the dealer whether your car is part of Acura's investigation or any related campaign before replacing parts.

issues.t: Flashing D indicator and rough shifting
issues.sym: The D or D4 indicator flashes, the check engine light comes on, the transmission shifts roughly, or more than one gear light shows at once.
issues.why: A fault in the transmission range sensor (code P26C3), sometimes caused by debris, can confuse the transmission computer. RepairPal also lists rough shifting with a flashing D4 light for these years.
issues.next: Have the codes read promptly. A dealer can check the range sensor under the related bulletin before any major transmission work.

issues.t: Tires slowly lose air
issues.sym: The low tire pressure light keeps coming back and one or more tires need air every few weeks.
issues.why: Acura issued bulletins on slow air leaks for these RLX and RLX Hybrid years, including corrosion of the valve stems from road salt.
issues.next: Have the tire shop check the valve stems and wheel bead area. Ask the dealer about the related bulletins.

issues.t: Rear lower control arm bolts can loosen (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking from the rear, or the car feels loose or hard to control.
issues.why: The bolts holding the rear lower control arms on some 2014 RLXs were not tightened correctly and can work loose.
issues.next: Confirm the recall was done. The dealer replaces the bolts for free. NHTSA recall number: 13V-622.
